file_browser.title: Library screen
file_browser.summary: How the Kobo's list of books and folders looks and behaves, and where certain files are saved.
file_browser.affects: You will see the change on the Kobo's home screen with your books and folders, usually the next time the list refreshes.

defaults_reflowable.title: Page layout for new books
defaults_reflowable.summary: Starting page layout (margins, text size, spacing, contrast) for normal ebooks such as EPUB.
defaults_reflowable.affects: Only books you open for the first time after the change start with these values; books you have already opened keep their own layout.

fonts_typography.title: Fonts and word breaking
fonts_typography.summary: Which fonts new ebooks use and how words are split and lined up at the ends of lines.
fonts_typography.affects: Most of these only change books opened for the first time after the change; books you have already opened keep their own settings.

defaults_fixed.title: PDFs and comics
defaults_fixed.summary: Starting view for PDFs, scanned books and comics, whose pages have a fixed layout.
defaults_fixed.affects: Only PDFs and comics opened for the first time after the change start this way; normal ebooks are not affected, and files you have already opened keep their own view.

shorten_home_dir.label: Show home folder as "Home"
shorten_home_dir.help: When on, the top of the library screen shows your home folder simply as "Home" instead of its full storage path. Purely cosmetic.
shorten_home_dir.example: On: the title bar reads "Home" instead of "/mnt/onboard".

lock_home_folder.help: When on, you cannot go up out of your home folder in the library screen, so you stay among your books and never wander into system folders.
lock_home_folder.example: Turn it on if you keep ending up in strange system folders by tapping ".." by accident.

file_ask_to_open.label: Ask before opening a book
file_ask_to_open.help: When on, tapping a book first asks "Open this file?" with Open and Cancel, instead of opening it straight away.
file_ask_to_open.example: Useful if you often open books by accident while scrolling.

show_parent_folder.label: Show "go up" entry in folders
show_parent_folder.help: When on, each folder starts with a ".." entry you can tap to go back up one folder. When off, that entry is hidden and you go back another way.

collection_show_mark.label: Mark books that are in a collection
collection_show_mark.help: When on, books that you have added to a collection (such as Favorites) get a small mark in the library list.

show_flat_view.label: Show all books in one list
show_flat_view.help: When on, a folder shows every book from all its subfolders together in one long list, without the folders. May need a restart of the reader app to take effect.
show_flat_view.example: On: if your books are split into author folders, you see all of them at once on the home screen.

show_hidden.help: When on, the library also shows hidden files and folders (names starting with a dot), which are normally system files. Best left off. May need a restart to take effect.

show_unsupported.label: Show files that cannot be opened
show_unsupported.help: When on, the library also lists files the Kobo cannot read (for example .txt notes from other apps or random downloads). When off, only readable books are shown. May need a restart to take effect.

collate.label: Sort books by
collate.help: Chooses the order of books in the library list. The new order shows the next time the list refreshes.
collate.example: Choose "Last read" to keep the books you are reading now at the top.

reverse_collate.label: Reverse sort order
reverse_collate.help: Flips the library order upside down, for example Z to A, or oldest read first.

collate_mixed.label: Mix folders in with books
collate_mixed.help: When off, folders are always listed first and books after them. When on, folders and books are sorted together in one list.

items_per_page.label: Books per page (list view)
items_per_page.help: How many lines the library list shows on one page when it is in the plain list view (without covers). More lines means smaller text per line. Does not change the cover view.
items_per_page.example: Set it to 10: fewer, larger entries per page, easier to tap.

items_font_size.label: Text size in list view
items_font_size.help: Text size of book names in the plain list view (without covers). If not set, the Kobo picks a size to fit the number of books per page.

items_multilines_show_more_text.label: Shrink text to fit long names
items_multilines_show_more_text.help: When on, long book names in the plain list view use a smaller text so more of the name fits, instead of being cut off.

show_file_in_bold.label: Which books are shown in bold
show_file_in_bold.help: In the plain list view, chooses which books are highlighted in bold. If not set, books you have never opened are shown in bold, so new arrivals stand out.

keyvalues_per_page.label: Lines per page in info screens
keyvalues_per_page.help: How many lines fit on one page in information screens such as book details and some settings lists, when the Kobo is held upright. Higher means smaller text. If not set, the Kobo picks a size for its screen.

keyvalues_per_page_landscape.label: Lines per page in info screens (sideways)
keyvalues_per_page_landscape.help: Same as the line above, but for when the screen is turned sideways. Your Kobo has no rotation sensor, so this only matters if you rotate the screen by hand.

download_dir.label: Folder for downloaded books
download_dir.help: The folder where books downloaded from an online catalogue are saved. If not set, the Kobo uses the last folder you picked. Must be a folder path on the Kobo.

inbox_dir.label: Folder for books from Calibre
inbox_dir.help: The folder where books sent wirelessly from the Calibre program on a computer are saved. Only matters if you use Calibre's wireless sending.

screenshot_dir.help: The folder where screenshots you take on the Kobo are saved. If not set, they go into a screenshots folder inside the reader app's own folder.

copt_rotation_mode.label: Screen rotation
copt_rotation_mode.help: Which way new books are shown on the screen. Your Kobo has no rotation sensor, so this is the only way to read sideways or upside down.
copt_rotation_mode.example: Choose 90 degrees to read a new book with the Kobo held sideways.

copt_visible_pages.label: Two pages side by side
copt_visible_pages.help: When on, the text is shown as two pages next to each other, like an open book. Only works when the screen is turned sideways and in page mode.

copt_sync_t_b_page_margins.label: Same top and bottom margin
copt_sync_t_b_page_margins.help: When on, the top and bottom margins are kept equal, so changing one changes the other and the text sits centred on the page.

copt_t_page_margin.help: Empty space above the text on each page. Higher values give a wider white strip at the top and fewer lines per page.
copt_t_page_margin.example: Set it to 30: a calmer page with more space at the top.

copt_b_page_margin.help: Empty space below the text on each page. Higher values give a wider white strip at the bottom and fewer lines per page.

copt_view_mode.label: Pages or scrolling
copt_view_mode.help: Page splits the book into separate pages you turn one by one, like paper. Continuous lets you scroll the text up and down like a web page.

copt_block_rendering_mode.label: How closely to follow the book's design
copt_block_rendering_mode.help: Controls how much of the publisher's page design is used. "Book" is a safe middle ground; "Web" follows the design most closely but can leave odd gaps or cut-off text; "Flat" and "Legacy" are simpler and plainer.

copt_render_dpi.label: Size of pictures and fixed sizes
copt_render_dpi.help: Scales pictures and anything the book sets to a fixed size (in centimetres or pixels). Higher values make pictures and such elements larger; "off" ignores fixed sizes. Normal text size is set separately.
copt_render_dpi.example: Set 167 if pictures in your books look tiny.

copt_line_spacing.help: Space between lines of text, as a percentage. Above 100% spreads the lines apart; below 100% packs them closer together.
copt_line_spacing.example: Set line spacing to 120%: lines sit a little further apart, easier on tired eyes.

copt_font_size.label: Text size
copt_font_size.help: The starting text size for new books. Higher numbers mean bigger letters and fewer words per page.
copt_font_size.example: Set 26 instead of 22 for noticeably larger, easier-to-read text.

copt_word_expansion.label: Letter spacing to fill lines
copt_word_expansion.help: When a line is stretched to reach both edges and the gaps between words get too wide, this allows a little extra space between letters instead. 0 means never; higher values allow more.
copt_word_expansion.example: Set 5%: fewer big holes between words on narrow lines.

copt_cjk_width_scaling.label: Width of Chinese/Japanese/Korean characters
copt_cjk_width_scaling.help: Makes Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters a bit wider, as a percentage. Has no effect on books in other languages.

copt_font_gamma.label: Text darkness
copt_font_gamma.help: How dark and crisp the text looks. Higher values make letters darker and bolder-looking; lower values make them lighter and greyer.
copt_font_gamma.example: Choose 1.45 if text looks a bit faint in daylight.

copt_font_base_weight.label: Text thickness
copt_font_base_weight.help: Makes all letters thinner or thicker. 0 is normal; positive values thicken the letters (up to bold), negative values make them thinner. Works best with fonts that come in several weights.
copt_font_base_weight.example: Set +0.5: slightly heavier letters that are easier to read on e-ink.

copt_font_hinting.label: Letter sharpening
copt_font_hinting.help: Adjusts letter shapes slightly so they line up with the screen's dots and look sharper. "Auto" usually looks best; differences are small.

copt_font_kerning.label: Spacing between letter pairs
copt_font_kerning.help: Kerning is fine-tuning the gap between certain letter pairs (like "AV") so words look even. "Best" looks nicest and joins letters like "fi" together; "off" is plainest.

copt_status_line.label: Extra status line at the top
copt_status_line.help: When on, a thin line with information such as page and time is shown at the top of the page. The normal status bar at the bottom is separate and not affected.

copt_embedded_css.label: Use the publisher's styling
copt_embedded_css.help: When on, the book's own design (indents, headings, spacing chosen by the publisher) is used. When off, books get a plain, uniform look.
copt_embedded_css.example: Turn it off if a publisher's layout has tiny text or strange spacing you cannot fix otherwise.

copt_embedded_fonts.label: Use the book's own fonts
copt_embedded_fonts.help: When on, fonts that come inside the book are used. When off, your chosen font is used for everything.
copt_embedded_fonts.example: Turn it off if you want every book in the same font you like.

copt_smooth_scaling.label: Picture quality
copt_smooth_scaling.help: How pictures inside the book are resized. "Best" looks smoother but is a little slower; "Fast" is quicker but pictures can look rough.

copt_nightmode_images.label: Invert pictures in night mode
copt_nightmode_images.help: Only matters when night mode (white text on black) is on. When on, pictures are inverted too so they match the dark page; turn it off if pictures look wrong, such as photos or diagrams.

copt_overlap_lines.label: Lines repeated when scrolling
copt_overlap_lines.help: Only in continuous scrolling with page overlap turned on: how many lines from the previous screen are repeated at the top of the next one, so you do not lose your place.

copt_css.label: Default book style
copt_css.help: The basic style sheet (a set of layout rules) used for books that have no style of their own chosen yet. Leave it empty unless you know which style you want.

copt_fb2_css.label: Default style for FB2 books
copt_fb2_css.help: Same as the default book style, but only for books in the FB2 format, which is common for Russian ebooks. Not relevant for EPUB books.

txt_preformatted.label: Plain text files: auto-detect layout
txt_preformatted.help: Only for plain .txt files. If not set, each line of the file is shown exactly as written. When auto-detect is on, the Kobo tries to find paragraphs and headings to make the text read like a book.

cre_font.label: Default font
cre_font.help: The font new books start with. Enter the font name exactly as it appears in the Kobo's font menu. If empty, Noto Serif is used.
cre_font.example: Set it to "Literata" to read every new book in Literata.

fallback_font.help: The font used for characters your main font does not have, for example Chinese or rare symbols. Usually best left as it is.

monospace_font.label: Font for computer code
monospace_font.help: The fixed-width font (every letter the same width) used for computer code or typewriter-style text in books.

cre_font_family_ignore_font_names.label: Prefer my fonts over publisher font names
cre_font_family_ignore_font_names.help: Some books ask for a specific named font before a general font type. When on, those names are ignored so the fonts you assigned to each font type are always used.

font_menu_use_font_face.label: Show font names in their own font
font_menu_use_font_face.help: When on, each font in the font menu is written in that font, so you can preview how it looks. Changes the menu only, not the book.

font_menu_sort_by_recently_selected.label: Recently used fonts first
font_menu_sort_by_recently_selected.help: When on, the font menu lists the fonts you picked most recently at the top instead of alphabetically.

additional_fallback_fonts.label: Use extra backup fonts
additional_fallback_fonts.help: When on, the Kobo also tries other installed fonts for characters missing from your main and fallback font, so fewer empty boxes appear in unusual text.

cre_adjusted_fallback_font_sizes.label: Match size of backup fonts
cre_adjusted_fallback_font_sizes.help: When on, characters drawn with a backup font are resized to match the main text, so they do not look too big or too small.

cre_monospace_scaling.label: Size of computer-code text
cre_monospace_scaling.help: Makes fixed-width text (such as computer code) larger or smaller compared to the rest, as a percentage.

hyphenation.label: Split long words at line ends
hyphenation.help: Hyphenation means breaking a word with a hyphen at the end of a line. When on, lines are more even with fewer big gaps between words; when off, words are never split.
hyphenation.example: On: "reading" may become "read-" / "ing" across two lines.

hyph_left_hyphen_min.label: Minimum letters before a break
hyph_left_hyphen_min.help: Only when splitting words is on: the fewest letters that must stay on the first line before the hyphen. Higher values mean fewer, longer splits. If not set, the book language's usual rule is used.
hyph_left_hyphen_min.example: Set 3: "a-bout" will never happen, only splits like "abo-ut" or later.

hyph_right_hyphen_min.label: Minimum letters after a break
hyph_right_hyphen_min.help: Only when splitting words is on: the fewest letters that must move to the next line after the hyphen. Higher values avoid short leftovers. If not set, the book language's usual rule is used.

hyph_trust_soft_hyphens.label: Use the book's own split points
hyph_trust_soft_hyphens.help: Some books mark exactly where words may be split. When on, those marks are used first, and the Kobo's own rules only for words without marks.

hyph_force_algorithmic.label: Split words by general rules
hyph_force_algorithmic.help: When on, words are split using simple general rules instead of the language's dictionary of split points. Useful only when no dictionary exists for the book's language.

hyph_soft_hyphens_only.label: Only use the book's own split points
hyph_soft_hyphens_only.help: When on, words are split only where the book itself marks it, never by the Kobo's rules. Books without such marks will then have no split words.

hyph_user_dict.label: Use my own word-split list
hyph_user_dict.help: When on, your own list of how specific words should be split is used before the normal rules. Only useful if you have made such a list on the Kobo.

floating_punctuation.label: Let punctuation hang in the margin
floating_punctuation.help: When on, commas, full stops and quote marks at the edge of a line are pushed slightly into the margin, so the text edge looks straighter, as in fine printed books.

text_lang_embedded_langs.label: Follow language marks inside the book
text_lang_embedded_langs.help: When on, if a book marks some passages as another language (say, a French quote in an English novel), word splitting and other language rules follow that mark for those passages.

text_lang_default.label: Always use this language for text rules
text_lang_default.help: Forces one language for word splitting and similar rules in every new book, ignoring the language the book says it is in. Use a short code such as en-US, nb or tr. If empty, the book's own language is used, else English.
text_lang_default.example: Set "nb" if you only read Norwegian books and some are wrongly marked as English.

text_lang_fallback.label: Language when the book has none
text_lang_fallback.help: The language used for word splitting and similar rules only when a book does not say which language it is in. Use a short code such as en-US, nb or tr.
text_lang_fallback.example: Set "tr" so unlabelled Turkish books still get proper word splitting.

cre_partial_rerendering.label: Faster re-layout after changes
cre_partial_rerendering.help: When on, after you change font or size the Kobo only re-lays out the part of the book you are reading first, so you can keep reading sooner. Turn it off only if you see layout glitches.

page_overlap_enable.label: Repeat lines when scrolling
page_overlap_enable.help: Only in continuous scrolling: when on, a few lines from the previous screen stay visible at the top of the next, so you do not lose your place.

page_overlap_style.label: How repeated lines are marked
page_overlap_style.help: Only when repeating lines while scrolling is on: how the repeated lines from the previous screen are marked so you can tell where new text starts.

kopt_rotation_mode.label: Screen rotation (PDFs)
kopt_rotation_mode.help: Which way new PDFs and comics are shown. Your Kobo has no rotation sensor; sideways can help with wide pages.

kopt_trim_page.label: Cut off empty page edges
kopt_trim_page.help: Only for PDFs and comics: removes blank white borders around the page so the content fills more of the screen. "Auto" finds the content by itself.
kopt_trim_page.example: Auto: a PDF with wide white margins shows bigger, easier-to-read text.

options.2: Automatic within an area you choose

kopt_page_margin.label: Margin around PDF pages
kopt_page_margin.help: Only for PDFs and comics: white space added around the page after trimming and zooming. Higher values give more space at the edges.

kopt_auto_straighten.label: Straighten tilted scans
kopt_auto_straighten.help: Only for scanned PDFs: tries to rotate pages that were scanned at a slant, by up to the chosen angle. 0 means off.

kopt_zoom_overlap_h.label: Overlap when moving sideways
kopt_zoom_overlap_h.help: Only for zoomed-in PDFs read piece by piece: how much of the previous piece is still visible when you move left or right, so you do not lose your place.

kopt_zoom_overlap_v.label: Overlap when moving down
kopt_zoom_overlap_v.help: Only for zoomed-in PDFs read piece by piece: how much of the previous piece is still visible when you move up or down, so you do not lose your place.

kopt_zoom_mode_type.label: Fit page to screen
kopt_zoom_mode_type.help: Only for PDFs and comics: whether the page is sized to show it whole, to fill the screen width, or to fill the screen height.
kopt_zoom_mode_type.example: Width: text is bigger, and you scroll down within each page.

kopt_zoom_factor.label: Manual zoom amount
kopt_zoom_factor.help: Only for PDFs and comics when "Zoom to" is set to manual: how much the page is enlarged. 1.5 means one and a half times bigger.

kopt_zoom_mode_genus.label: Zoom to
kopt_zoom_mode_genus.help: Only for PDFs and comics: what the Kobo zooms in on. "Page" shows the page; "Content" ignores blank edges; "Columns" or "Rows" splits the page into parts you read one at a time.
kopt_zoom_mode_genus.example: Columns: a two-column scientific PDF is shown one column at a time, much larger.

kopt_zoom_direction.label: Reading order when zoomed
kopt_zoom_direction.help: Only for zoomed-in PDFs and comics read piece by piece: the order in which the pieces are shown. Normal books are left to right, top to bottom; manga is usually right to left.
kopt_zoom_direction.example: Choose "Right to left, top to bottom" for Japanese manga.

options.7: Left to right, then top to bottom
options.6: Top to bottom, then left to right
options.5: Left to right, then bottom to top
options.4: Bottom to top, then left to right
options.3: Bottom to top, then right to left
options.2: Right to left, then bottom to top
options.1: Top to bottom, then right to left
options.0: Right to left, then top to bottom

kopt_page_scroll.label: Pages or scrolling (PDFs)
kopt_page_scroll.help: Only for PDFs and comics: "Pages" shows one page at a time; "Continuous" lets you scroll through pages like a web page.

kopt_page_gap_height.label: Gap between pages when scrolling
kopt_page_gap_height.help: Only for PDFs in continuous scrolling: the thickness of the gap between one page and the next.

kopt_line_spacing.label: Line spacing (re-flowed PDFs)
kopt_line_spacing.help: Only when re-flow is on for a PDF: space between lines of the re-arranged text.

kopt_justification.label: Text alignment (re-flowed PDFs)
kopt_justification.help: Only when re-flow is on for a PDF: how lines are lined up. "Justify" makes both edges straight; "Auto" tries to copy the original document.

kopt_font_size.label: Text size (re-flowed PDFs)
kopt_font_size.help: Only when re-flow is on for a PDF: enlarges or shrinks the text compared with the original. 1.0 is the original size, 1.3 is 30% bigger.

kopt_word_spacing.label: Word gap (re-flowed PDFs)
kopt_word_spacing.help: Only when re-flow is on for a PDF: how much space is left between words.

kopt_text_wrap.label: Re-flow PDF text
kopt_text_wrap.help: Re-flow means pulling the text out of a PDF and re-arranging it to fit the Kobo's screen, like a normal ebook. Makes small PDF text readable, but tables, pictures and formatting can come out messy.
kopt_text_wrap.example: On: an A4 PDF becomes readable without zooming, but a page of formulas may look jumbled.

kopt_contrast.label: Darkness (PDFs)
kopt_contrast.help: Only for PDFs and comics: makes the page darker. 1 is unchanged; higher values make faint or grey text darker and easier to read.
kopt_contrast.example: Set 1.5 for an old scan with pale grey text.

kopt_white_threshold.label: Turn light grey into white
kopt_white_threshold.help: Only for PDFs and comics: anything lighter than this level is shown as pure white. 255 means off; lower values clean up grey backgrounds but can wash out light details.

kopt_page_opt.label: Remove watermarks and grey backgrounds
kopt_page_opt.help: Only for PDFs and comics: tries to remove faint watermarks and grey backgrounds, making the page plain black and white with more contrast.

kopt_background_cleanup.label: Black and white cleanup
kopt_background_cleanup.help: Only for PDFs: shows just the essentials in black and white and skips extra layers, for better contrast and faster page turns. Especially useful for scanned books from the Internet Archive.

kopt_hw_dithering.label: Smoother greys (screen)
kopt_hw_dithering.help: Only for PDFs and comics: dithering means drawing shades of grey as fine dot patterns, so pictures look smoother on e-ink. This version uses the screen's own built-in method, if it has one.

kopt_sw_dithering.label: Smoother greys (software)
kopt_sw_dithering.help: Only for PDFs and comics: draws shades of grey as fine dot patterns, calculated by the reader app, so photos and drawings show less banding. Can slow page turns slightly.

kopt_quality.label: Quality (re-flowed PDFs)
kopt_quality.help: Only when re-flow is on for a PDF: how carefully text and pictures are extracted. Higher gives sharper results but pages take longer to prepare.

kopt_doc_language.label: Language for text recognition
kopt_doc_language.help: Only for scanned PDFs: the language the Kobo assumes when it reads text from page images (text recognition), for example when you select words. Uses a three-letter code such as eng, nor or tur. If empty, English is used.

kopt_forced_ocr.label: Always read text from the image
kopt_forced_ocr.help: Only for PDFs: when on, selecting text always uses text recognition on the page image, even if the PDF already contains text. Turn on only if selecting text in a PDF gives garbled words.

kopt_writing_direction.label: Writing direction (re-flowed PDFs)
kopt_writing_direction.help: Only when re-flow is on for a PDF: the direction the original text is written in. Set to right-to-left for Arabic or Hebrew so the text is re-arranged correctly.

options.2: Top to bottom, columns right to left

kopt_defect_size.label: Ignore specks (re-flowed PDFs)
kopt_defect_size.help: Only when re-flow is on for a scanned PDF: how big a dust spot or ink speck may be before it is treated as a real character. Larger ignores bigger specks but may drop small dots like full stops.

kopt_detect_indent.label: Keep paragraph indents (re-flowed PDFs)
kopt_detect_indent.help: Only when re-flow is on for a PDF: whether paragraph indents from the original are kept. The reader app hides this option because it does not currently work, so changing it likely has no effect.

kopt_nightmode_document.label: Invert pages in night mode
kopt_nightmode_document.help: Only for PDFs and comics, and only when night mode (white on black) is on: whether the pages are inverted too. Off keeps pages as they are, which usually suits picture-heavy comics.

kopt_max_columns.label: Columns to look for (re-flowed PDFs)
kopt_max_columns.help: Only when re-flow is on for a PDF: the most text columns the Kobo looks for on a page. Set to 1 if normal full-width text gets wrongly split into columns.
